names: UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision
record.summary: UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois Street, a 347,500-sq-ft eye-care facility in three buildings (a 12-story tower with a 5-story south wing and a 3-story north wing) that SF YIMBY reported open on November 27, 2020, at a reported cost of about $237 million (SmithGroup architect). It stands on OCII plan block 33, between Third St and Illinois St: the City's address point for 490 Illinois St falls inside this outline, and UCSF's own 2025 campus map labels block 33 'Valley Center for Vision'. Its footprint here is approximate (see the shape's accuracy caveat).

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL BUILDING, APPROXIMATE BOUNDARY -- a real, standing structure clearly visible in Esri satellite imagery (not open land): UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois St. The City's official address point for 490 Illinois St (DataSF Addresses, address ID 743049, on Assessor parcel 8725001) lies inside this outline; UCSF's June 2025 CAC presentation map labels block 33, between Third St and Illinois St, 'VALLEY CENTER FOR VISION (33)'; and SF YIMBY (2020-11-27) places the facilities 'along 3rd Street, immediately across from the UCSF Medical Center'. Boundary is the edge of the open ground left between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes (following the estimated curb radius), with one corner redrawn to the real street angle (see the mapping log), not a hand-traced or surveyed building footprint. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Outlined as the ground left between DataSF's official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes, between 3rd St and Illinois St, south of 16th St. Pier & Point judged that this piece (12,421 sqm before cutting) covers two separate real buildings, not one, and cut it by hand at the visible gap between the two rooflines in Esri satellite imagery (lat 37.76578).

facts.value: 490 Illinois St: the City's address point (DataSF Addresses, address ID 743049) lies inside this record's outline, on Assessor parcel 8725001, which the Assessor itself addresses as 480 16th St.

changes.text: UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois St is the block 33 building between Third St and Illinois St, not the pair of buildings east of Illinois St that this project had listed under that name. The City's address point for 490 Illinois St falls inside the block 33 outline; UCSF's 2025 campus map labels block 33 'Valley Center for Vision'; SF YIMBY places the facility 'along 3rd Street, immediately across from the UCSF Medical Center'; and the two buildings east of Illinois St were already standing, about six stories tall, in the City's 2010 building survey. The block 33 record is renamed 'UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision' and now carries the 2017 Regents approval, the November 2020 opening, the $237 million cost, the SmithGroup design, the 347,500 sq ft size and the Caffe Central tenant. Its old page address redirects to the new one.

changes.text: The block 33 record said its identification as UCSF's Valley Center for Vision had no published source. UCSF's June 2025 CAC presentation (map updated December 2024) labels block 33 'VALLEY CENTER FOR VISION (33)', so the summary, caveat and map notes now cite it, along with OCII's 2019 Land Use Map. Because UCSF's map places the name on block 33, between Third St and Illinois St, the separate 490/499 Illinois St record east of Illinois St may be the one that is mislabelled; that record has not been changed and the question remains open. The record's own mapping log is now labelled as this project's narrative, the NAIP aerial credit names the USDA Farm Production and Conservation Business Center, and the Wikimedia aerial credit names only the Commons username Firstcultural.

open_questions: No source read gives the exact opening day: SF YIMBY reported the building open on November 27, 2020, without a date.

UCSF's news page for the January 2017 Regents approval could not be read (it refuses automated fetches, and no archived copy was found); the Regents date and the expected 2017-2019 schedule rest on earlier notes of that page, not a direct read. Its $237,000,000 budget and 12-, 5- and 3-story massing match SF YIMBY's article, which was read.
No opening date was found for Caffe Central at 490 Illinois St: the cafe's own page lists the location and its hours but gives no date.

OpenStreetMap labels one of the 409/499 Illinois St buildings across Illinois St (way 84821722, 6 levels, 28 m) as 490 Illinois St. The City's address point, UCSF's 2025 campus map and SF YIMBY's description all place the 12-story Valley Center for Vision here instead, so that label is not used.

Geometry: this building's east edge sits close to, but not necessarily exactly on, Illinois St's west curb line; it has not been checked against a building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, surveyed in 2010, predates the building).
